extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / readers of Mochizuki's IUT theory
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, structural properties, and functorial/compatibility requirements for various Hodge-theater-like objects (Θ-Hodge theaters, NF-bridges, D-Θ±-bridges, D-Θell-bridges, D-Θ±ell-Hodge theaters) and their morphisms within Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmüller theory. Includes torsor/ symmetry statements and transport of labelled cusps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphism / isomorphism of Θ-bridges
rubrics_metrics.description: An (iso)morphism between two Θ-bridges is a collection of arrows giving: a capsule-full poly-isomorphism between the respective capsules of F-prime-strips, a full poly-isomorphism between the respective F-prime-strips, and an isomorphism of Θ-Hodge theaters, all compatible in the evident sense with the poly-morphisms ψΘ and with the associated “(cid:8)(cid:8)(cid:9)” identifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compatibility must hold with the determining poly-morphisms ψΘ (for each bridge) and with the capsule identifications; composition of such morphisms is the evident composition. The capsule-full / full poly-isomorphism conditions are central (see §0 and Remark 3.6.2 for precise notions).

rubrics_metrics.name: ΘNF-Hodge theater (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ΘNF-Hodge theater (relative to given initial Θ-data) is a collection of data consisting of an NF-bridge and a Θ-bridge such that the associated data (the NF- and Θ-bridge data together with their associated maps) form a D-ΘNF-Hodge theater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An isomorphism of ΘNF-Hodge theaters is a pair of morphisms between the associated NF- and Θ-bridges that induce the same bijection between index sets of the respective capsules of F-prime-strips; composition of morphisms is as for the constituent bridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijectivity: isomorphisms of Θ-Hodge theaters ↔ D-prime-strips (Corollary 5.6(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed initial Θ-data, the natural functorially induced map from the set of isomorphisms between two Θ-Hodge theaters to the set of isomorphisms between the respective associated D-prime-strips is bijective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: the only data not contained in the associated F-prime-strip is certain global data which can be recovered functorially from the associated F-prime-strips (via the algorithm summarized in Remark 5.2.1); apply earlier corollaries to conclude bijectivity. This gives a criterion: to check isomorphism of Θ-Hodge theaters it suffices to check the induced isomorphism of associated D-prime-strips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijectivity for NF-bridges, Θ-bridges, ΘNF-Hodge theaters (Corollary 5.6(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The functorially induced map from isomorphisms between two NF-bridges (respectively two Θ-bridges; two ΘNF-Hodge theaters) to isomorphisms between the respective associated D-NF-bridges (respectively, associated D-Θ-bridges; associated D-ΘNF-Hodge theaters) is bijective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces questions about isomorphisms of the original (NF/Θ/ΘNF) objects to isomorphisms of their associated purely D-objects; use earlier Corollary 5.3 results for verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing torsor: capsule-full poly-isomorphisms (Corollary 5.6(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an NF-bridge and a Θ-bridge, the set of capsule-full poly-isomorphisms between the respective capsules of F-prime-strips which allow one to glue these bridges together into a ΘNF-Hodge theater forms an F_l-torsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically: choices of glueings are parameterized by a torsor under the finite field F_l; this quantifies the indeterminacy in forming ΘNF-Hodge theaters from given NF- and Θ-bridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: F±_l-group / F±_l-torsor and Aut+(T), Aut±(T) (Definition 6.1(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Define F_l^± := F_l × {±1} (semi-direct product) and an F_l^±-group to be a set E with a {±1}-orbit structure mapping to F_l; an F_l^±-torsor is a set T with an F_l^±-structure. Aut+(T) is the subgroup of automorphisms of T corresponding to 'positive automorphisms' (translations by elements of F_l); Aut±(T) is the full automorphism group (index-two extension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aut+(T) is an abelian group with natural F_l^±-group structure; Aut±(T) contains Aut+(T) with index 2. Use these to control signs and ±-symmetries in later constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: D± from D and LabCusp±(D_v) (Definition 6.1(ii)-(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-prime-strip D = {D_v}_v, one functorially constructs D^± = {D_v^±}_v, together with the notion of cusps and ±-label-classes of cusps LabCusp±(D_v). LabCusp±(D_v) carries a natural F_l^±-group structure, admits a zero element η0_v and a ±-canonical element η±_v (well-defined up to ±1), and there are natural bijections relating LabCusp±(D_v) to the usual LabCusp(D_v) modulo ±1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The construction uses π1(D_v) and group-theoretic algorithms (or π0 of neighborhoods at infinity for archimedean places). LabCusp± is compatible with actions of F_l and with functorial reconstructions of tempered Frobenioids; these labels will be the objects transported via bridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: +-full poly-isomorphism and α-signed +-full poly-isomorphism (Definition 6.1(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: A +-full poly-isomorphism between D-prime-strips D_v → D'_v is the Aut+(D_v)-orbit of an isomorphism. For the whole capsule D → D', the set of +-full poly-isomorphisms is naturally in bijection with {±1}^V, and the α-signed +-full poly-isomorphism is the one corresponding to α ∈ {±1}^V. A capsule-+-full poly-morphism is a poly-morphism determined by +-full poly-isomorphisms on constituents respecting an injection between index sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes the notion of isomorphisms up to positive automorphisms; used throughout to measure sign ambiguities and index-by-index choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and automorphisms of D(6)^± and their arithmetic meaning (Definition 6.1(v)-(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: One constructs a finite étale double cover D(6)^± → D(6) coming from l-torsion points of an elliptic curve E_F. There is an outer homomorphism Aut(D(6)^±) → GL_2(F_l)/{±1} whose image contains a Borel subgroup; Aut^±(D(6)^±) is the kernel of a natural surjection to F_l^±. Autcsp(D(6)^±) is subgroup fixing cusps, and quotient identifications give outer isomorphisms with Aut_K(X_K) etc. LabCusp±(D(6)^±) can be identified with F_l^±-torsor structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These identifications are reconstructible category-theoretically from D(6)^± and are used to define actions on cusps, index sets V^±, and to relate geometric automorphisms to the finite group symmetries used later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model base-Θ±-bridge construction and poly-automorphisms (Example 6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct tautological copies D_t of the tautological D-prime-strip indexed by t ∈ F_l and form the capsule D^± = {D_t}_t. Define positive +-full poly-isomorphisms φ_Θ^±_t: D_t → D and φ_Θ^±_± the collection. There are natural poly-automorphisms: −1_{F_l} acts by multiplying indices by −1 and flipping signs at all v; α ∈ {±1}^V acts by α-signed +-full poly-automorphisms on components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These model constructions give canonical examples and describe the basic symmetries (index sign flip and coordinatewise sign changes) one must account for when judging equivalence or building torsors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model base-Θell-bridge and equivariance (Example 6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using an identification LabCusp±(D(6)^±) ≃ F_l, build D^± and maps φ_Θell_t : D_t → D(6)^± for t ∈ F_l and the collection φ_Θell^±. There is a natural poly-action of F_l^± on D^± and D(6)^±; φ_Θell^± is equivariant for these poly-actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model exhibits how labelling of cusps by an F_l^±-torsor yields equivariant maps and how the arithmetic automorphism group acts on these models.

rubrics_metrics.name: D-Θ±-bridge, D-Θell-bridge, D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater (Definition 6.4(i)-(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A base-Θ±-bridge (D-Θ±-bridge) is a poly-morphism †DT → †D(cid:18) where T is an F_l^±-group and †DT is a capsule indexed by T such that there exist isomorphisms to the model objects (D(cid:18), D^±) matching F_l^±-structures. A base-Θell-bridge (D-Θell-bridge) is similar with T an F_l^±-torsor and target †D(6)^±. A D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater consists of a triple (†D(cid:18) ← †DT → †D(6)^±) with the appropriate structures; morphisms are pairs of compatible morphisms of the constituent bridges inducing the same poly-isomorphism between capsules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include existence of isomorphisms to fixed model data respecting the F_l^±-group/torsor structures; morphisms must be capsule-+-full poly-isomorphisms on the DT side and appropriate (Autcsp-orbit) poly-morphisms on the D(6)^± side. Composition is defined componentwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport of ±-label classes of cusps via base-bridges (Proposition 6.5(i)-(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater, for each v ∈ V and t ∈ T the D-Θell-bridge induces a well-defined bijection ζ^Θell_{v,t}: LabCusp±(D_{v,t}) → LabCusp±(D(6)^±) compatible with the F_l^±-torsor structures. These bijections glue across v to identify LabCusp±(D_t) as an F_l^±-torsor and produce a single bijection ζ^Θell_t: LabCusp±(D_t) → LabCusp±(D(6)^±). Similarly the D-Θ±-bridge induces bijections to LabCusp±(D(cid:18),v) and produces a global identification LabCusp±(D(cid:18)). The assignment t ↦ ζ^Θell_t(0) yields a bijection ζ^±: T → LabCusp±(D(6)^±) compatible with torsor structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These transport bijections are canonical (well-defined) and compatible with group/torsor actions; they are used to transfer cusp-label information between the capsule index set T and the arithmetic model D(6)^±. The behavior under post-composition by elements of Aut±(D(6)^±)/Autcsp is explicitly described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior under automorphisms: effect on transported bijections (Proposition 6.5(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: If α ∈ Aut±(D(6)^±)/Autcsp(D(6)^±) and one replaces φ_Θell^± by α◦φ_Θell^±, then the transported bijections ζ^Θell_t are changed by post-composition with the image of α in Aut±(LabCusp±(D(6)^±)) ≃ F_l^±.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This records how choices of automorphisms of the arithmetic target modify the identifications between T and LabCusp±; it quantifies the natural indeterminacy under the finite group action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism-sets as torsors and symmetry groups (Proposition 6.6(i)-(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed initial Θ-data: (i) the set of isomorphisms between two D-Θ±-bridges is a torsor over {±1} × {±1}^V (first factor from −1_{F_l}-type automorphisms, second from coordinatewise α∈{±1}^V); (ii) the set of isomorphisms between two D-Θell-bridges is a torsor over a finite group with an outer isomorphism to F_l^±, and maps bijectively to the set of isomorphisms of F_l^±-torsors between index sets; (iii) the set of isomorphisms between two D-Θ±ell-Hodge theaters is a {±1}-torsor and maps bijectively to isomorphisms of F_l^±-groups between index sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These torsor statements quantify the finite ambiguity in comparing such objects and identify the controlling symmetry groups; when checking uniqueness or counting automorphisms, use these torsor descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing torsor for D-Θ± and D-Θell to D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater (Proposition 6.6(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-Θ±-bridge and a D-Θell-bridge, the set of capsule-+-full poly-isomorphisms between their capsules that allow gluing to form a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater is a torsor over F_l^± × ({±1} × {±1}^V), where the F_l^± factor corresponds to the action described in the D-Θell case and the {±1}×{±1}^V corresponds to the automorphisms from Example 6.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the full finite-group parameterization of choices when attempting to glue two base-bridges into a combined Hodge theater; use this to enumerate or normalize choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial construction from D-Θell-bridge to D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater (Proposition 6.6(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-Θell-bridge, there is a functorial algorithm (relatively simple) that constructs, up to an F_l^±-indeterminacy, a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater whose underlying D-Θell-bridge is the given one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a constructive method to 'lift' a D-Θell-bridge to a full D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater, with the only ambiguity controlled by the finite F_l^± group; see Example 6.2 for explicit models.

rubrics_metrics.name: From D-Θ±-bridge to D-Θ-bridge algorithm (Proposition 6.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-Θ±-bridge †DT → †D(cid:18), by replacing †DT with the quotient †DT(|T|), identifying †D(cid:18) with †D_0 via φ_Θ^±, replacing +-full poly-morphisms at v∈V_good by full poly-morphisms and at v∈V_bad by group-theoretic poly-morphisms (per Example 4.4), one obtains functorially a D-Θ-bridge †DT(|T|) → †D_> well-defined up to unique isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a canonical way to forget the ±-structure and recover a multiplicative-type bridge; in the passage index-fibers of size two are merged so two D-prime-strips map to one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetries from forgetful functors (Proposition 6.8(i)-(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The functor forgetting parts of a D-Θ±ell-Hodge theater yields outputs with large symmetry groups: (i) forgetting to the underlying D-Θell-bridge yields an F_l^±-symmetry acting doubly transitively on the index set T; (ii) associating the l^±-capsule gives an S_{l^±}-symmetry acting transitively on |T| (forgetting labels in Fl/{±1}); (iii) composing with mono-analyticization preserves these symmetry properties for the analytic-capsule outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statements constrain the automorphism orbits of the forgetful images and indicate how much information is lost by forgetting labels: e.g., forgetting the exact element of Fl attached to an index leaves l^± possibilities per index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processions of base-prime-strips and associated functor (Proposition 6.9(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a D-Θ±-bridge with underlying capsule †DT, one can form an l^±-procession Prc(†DT) of D-prime-strips (a chain of subcapsules corresponding to subsets S^±_1 ⊆ ... ⊆ S^±_{l^±} = |Fl| under the bijection |T|→|Fl|). The assignment †φΘ^± ↦ Prc(†DT) defines a natural functor from the category of D-Θ±-bridges to the category of processions of D-prime-strips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This combinatorial construction organizes the capsule components into a labelled procession (illustrated in Fig. 6.2) and is natural with respect to isomorphisms of D-Θ±-bridges.
